name: Kennen, Heart of the Tempest
howItPlays: You play cards out of your trash and other zones instead of only your hand to charge up Kennen, then cash that charge in to give one of your units extra might for the turn and swing a fight your way. You spend early turns setting up removal and small units, then look for a turn where several charged effects land at once and take over the game.
whyYou: You like decks packed with options where you are usually holding an answer for whatever the opponent tries. You enjoy the moment several small edges line up into one turn that swings hard in your favor, and you do not mind that some games hinge on drawing the right card at the right time. If flexible, spell-heavy play with an explosive payoff sounds fun, Kennen is for you.
ratingNotes:
pace 6.5: riftbound.gg says Kennen wins by controlling the early board then pivoting to an explosive turn rather than racing from turn one; riftstorm.gg's counter guide independently rates speed 'Mid-range,' scoring mainly on turns three to six.
stance 6.5: riftbound.gg says the deck plays 'proactively early, then reactively opportunistic,' and riftstorm.gg's counter guide calls it 'primarily proactive,' describing 'a two-step turn: play or replay a card from outside the hand so Kennen becomes Empowered' before converting that into an attack; the Vendetta launch roundup instead calls it a 'Reactive-Proactive hybrid,' so this sits just proactive of center.
complexity 7: riftbound.gg calls it only moderately complex, but riftstorm.gg's counter guide calls it 'moderate to high,' and its separate Vendetta launch roundup rates complexity 'Very High,' calling Kennen 'sequencing-intensive' since 'disciplined pilots must know when to bank trash value and when to fight immediately'; this file weights the two more detailed, more recent reads.
variance 8: riftbound.gg describes 'explosive play patterns' and discounted key cards; riftstorm.gg's counter guide independently calls variance 'high,' saying 'a single turn can convert accumulated resources into decisive board leverage'; this is the highest variance call in this batch.
Legend ability: playing a card from anywhere other than your hand Empowers Kennen; Action, disempower and exhaust, to give a unit Assault 2 for the turn.
Confidence: high. Three write-ups read in full (riftbound.gg's dedicated guide, riftstorm.gg's Kennen counter guide, and riftstorm.gg's Vendetta launch roundup), all agreeing on a Tempo-leaning, high-variance read even though they differ on exactly how proactive and how complex it is. Domains are Order/Chaos, an opposite pair, so per project convention the chaos-order coordinate is 0 by design even though the guides read the deck as a Chaos/Order hybrid plan.
